subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Explain the terms gangue and slag.

verification.note: Unit 6 (Metallurgy) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book pp.79-82, which prints the question and a model answer. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. EQUATION CHECKED: FeO + SiO₂ → FeSiO₃ balances as printed (Fe 1=1, Si 1=1, O 3=3). BOOK GAP: the printed answer does not say that the slag is lighter than the molten metal and floats; that is what makes the slag removable and it is added here.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Gangue
lines: Gangue is the earthy and rocky impurity
present along with the mineral in an ore.
Sand, clay and rock fragments are common
It contains no metal that is wanted, and
it must be removed before the ore is
steps.why: Gangue is defined by where it is, not by what it is made of: it is whatever comes with the ore that is not the mineral. Naming a couple of examples shows that it is earthy material and not a compound of the metal.
common_mistakes: Calling gangue the impurity in the metal. Gangue is in the ore, before extraction; impurities in the metal are removed later by refining.
Confusing gangue with slag. Gangue is present before the flux is added; slag is what is formed after.
steps.memory_tip: Gangue comes with the ore. Slag is made in the furnace.
steps.margin_note: One line of definition plus one example is enough for this mark.

steps.label: Slag
lines: When a flux is added it combines with the
gangue and forms an easily fusible
The slag is lighter than the molten metal,
floats on it and is drawn off.
steps.why: The slag is defined by the reaction that makes it, so the flux has to be in the definition. The example equation shows all three terms at once: FeO is the gangue, SiO₂ the flux and FeSiO₃ the slag.
common_mistakes: Saying slag is the pure metal. Slag is the waste layer floating on the metal.
Writing the definition without the flux. Gangue on its own does not become slag.
steps.memory_tip: Flux plus gangue gives slag, and the slag floats.
steps.margin_note: The one-line equation with the three terms labelled under it answers both halves of this question.

insider_note: Gangue and slag are two ends of the same step. Write FeO + SiO₂ → FeSiO₃ once and label all three terms under it.
